review.notes: Complete actual function/table/view exports filtered only by worker database_name, reconciled with Rust schema registration. Seventeen logical names, overloads/aliases merged. File-reading and stream/ID/time functions remain in denominator despite not being demonstrated. Current raw COPY support advertises no extra named SQL function/table/view in these exports; no COPY handler name has been filtered out. Selected scalar adapters and underlying codec/validation/field/type logic are unchanged from v0.4.0 to current public baseline; seq/lib integration differs. Current catalog uses existing previously validated native binary, without rebuilding.

review.purpose: Construct explicit typed BSON fixtures, then restore canonical/relaxed representations for fidelity comparison.
review.finding: Twelve original documents use explicit number/date/binary/identifier wrappers; saved BLOBs let SQL compare complete bytes. Original inputs remain fixed while the selected representation changes.

review.purpose: Measure both type-aware and display-oriented JSON representations without conflating text size with fidelity.
review.finding: Literal mode branches materialize canonical and relaxed text. UTF8 byte totals remain a fixed comparison while the selected fidelity matrix changes; wrappers can preserve information at a size cost, not a measured latency cost.

review.purpose: Detect a changed BSON leaf type even when extracted text remains equal.
review.finding: Canonical output preserves all twelve inspected types and bytes. Relaxed output narrows the two small Int64 fields to Int32 while their text remains 7; binary subtype is retained in the full reported type.

review.purpose: Separate leaf text from type/whole-document identity and distinguish missing values.
review.finding: Literal top-level/nested paths return comparable strings. A separate control shows explicit BSON null and string null both display as text null, whereas absent fields, invalid documents and missing documents require distinct context.

review.purpose: Diagnose unusable bytes before interpreting a missing field result.
review.finding: The invalid short blob reports false with kind truncated; missing document returns NULL, and an absent leaf in a structurally valid document retains true. These are byte-level checks rather than application-schema checks.

review.purpose: Use a structural triage flag alongside diagnostic reasons while preserving NULL input.
review.finding: Known valid documents return true even if the inspected field is absent, malformed bytes false, and SQL NULL remains NULL. The table separates missing data from a failed structural check.

review.purpose: Interpret observed BSON type labels through the release registry and select the dimensions of a fidelity audit.
review.finding: All observed categories join their type byte/class/wrapper; numeric width wrappers explain why leaf-type checks matter. Binary suffix removal applies only to registry lookup, preserving the original subtype-bearing type string.

review.purpose: Expose field-order differences that a set-of-fields or leaf-only comparison would miss.
review.finding: Two documents with equal named values show key sequences [a,b] and [b,a], different canonical JSON order and unequal complete BSON bytes. Canonical Extended JSON is not universal key sorting.

review.purpose: Cross-check JSON-based construction with a native typed SQL input.
review.finding: Encoding a STRUCT containing BIGINT 7 yields BSON long and byte-identical output to the explicit numberLong wrapper control. This is one tested construction route, not a guarantee for all SQL types.

review.purpose: Identify the SQL output type of a rich BSON decoding path before treating it as typed columns.
review.finding: decode returns VARCHAR containing canonical Extended JSON with numberLong metadata. The typed BSON value and SQL display type are distinct, and its text agrees with the canonical JSON control.
